extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue et al., MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI, arXiv:2311.16502, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages: selecting subjects based on visual input adoption, recruiting over 50 university students as annotators to collect questions from textbooks and online resources, and performing data quality control through duplicate identification, format checking, and difficulty categorization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, and textbooks from six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data cleaning involved identifying potential duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by author review. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. Approximately 10% of problems classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard). Problems classified as 'very easy' were excluded. Questions were formatted into JSON files with standardized naming conventions for questions and images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students specializing in various majors collected multimodal questions. They were instructed to adhere to copyright regulations and avoid data from sites prohibiting copy/redistribution. Questions were annotated with question type, options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanations. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various majors and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/. A live-updating leaderboard is available. Version history includes updates to model results and fixes to typos and case studies.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which is defined as reaching at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults. It highlights challenges in multimodal understanding and reasoning, pointing towards areas needing further research and model enhancement to build next-generation multimodal foundation models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI as defined by Morris et al. [57].
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs). It is designed to evaluate expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning across 30 subjects and 183 subfields.
